channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: British Pound rebounds as soft JOLTS, Oil fall pressures the USD
item.description: The Pound Sterling recovers some ground against the US Dollar on Tuesday, up 0.14%, as US jobs data was softer than expected but confirmed the strength of the labour market, with layoffs being little changed. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3451 after rebounding at 1.3419.

item.title: Euro holds above 1.1500 on Hormuz reopening hopes and softer US jobs data
item.description: EUR/USD holds firm above 1.1500 on Tuesday as traders assess the latest developments surrounding US-Iran talks and the possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Silver advances amid Hormuz reopening hopes
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades with a mildly positive tone near $59.50 per troy ounce on Tuesday, up 2% for the day, but falling from recent highs and leaving the metal locked in a tight range.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Rally questioned as safe-haven role tested – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes the US Dollar (USD) has been the weakest G10 currency over the past week, with US Dollar Index (DXY) down about 2% from late July.

item.title: Asia FX: Yen-led winners and export backdrop – MUFG
item.description: Michael Wan at MUFG explains that South Korean Won (KRW), Thai Baht (THB), Singapore Dollar (SGD) and, to a smaller extent, Philippine Peso (PHP) are the main Asian FX beneficiaries if Japanese Yen strength persists, given their higher sensitivity to USD/JPY.

item.title: Euro: Consolidation below resistance against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s analysts observe that the Euro is consolidating around the 1.15 area against the Dollar, with limited Eurozone data to drive price action.

item.title: Japanese Yen stalls amid soft JOLTS data
item.description: USD/JPY trades on the back foot near the 157.40 area during Tuesday's American session as the Japanese Yen (JPY) builds on the gains secured over the past week.

item.title: Canada: Trade surplus hits four-year high – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada’s (NBC) Jocelyn Paquet reports Canada’s merchandise trade surplus in goods reached a four-year high of C$3.86 billion in June, beating expectations.

item.title: Gold recovers as Hormuz reopening hopes drag US Dollar, Oil prices lower
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) catches a fresh bid on Tuesday as traders react to encouraging headlines about the possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,087, recovering from an intraday low near $4,042.

item.title: Fed's Paulson: Underlying inflation is too high
item.description: Anna Paulson, President of the Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Philadelphia, said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday that underlying inflation remains too high and that monetary policy needs to stay mildly restrictive, adding that the current environment likely meets that description.

item.title: Australian Dollar climbs above 0.7000 as hopes of an Iran deal lift risk sentiment
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7035 on Tuesday at the time of writing, up 0.50% on the day. The pair is supported by improving market sentiment after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that an agreement with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday.

item.title: United States: Growth impulse questioned – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered analysts Dan Pan and Steve Englander discuss the Federal Reserve’s Financial Conditions Impulse on Growth (FCI-G) index, noting it was highly accommodative in May 2026 and still supportive after the July FOMC.

item.title: United States JOLTS Job Openings decline to 7.35 million in June
item.description: The number of job openings stood at 7.359 million in June, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Tuesday. This print followed the 7.537 million openings reported in May and came in slightly below the market expectation of 7.4 million.

item.title: US Dollar: Dip after FOMC but strength expected – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists discuss the US Dollar (USD) reaction to the July Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, where the Federal Reserve (Fed) kept rates at 3.50-3.75% despite some dissent for a hike.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens as Oil prices slide on US-Iran deal hopes
item.description: USD/CAD reverses its earlier losses on Tuesday as falling Oil prices weigh on the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) following comments from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on US-Iran talks.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention focus and Dollar supply - BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights ongoing market focus on Japanese Yen intervention, noting authorities stepped back from action overnight as Tokyo seeks to preserve its International Monetary Fund (IMF) free‑floating status.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Labor market soft, RBNZ hike eyed – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Australia/NZ macro team sees New Zealand Employment growth at 0.1% q/q in Q2, insufficient to match population gains. They expect the Unemployment Rate to rise to 5.4%, returning to its recent cycle high and aligning with the RBNZ’s May forecast.

item.title: US Dollar: FOMC fallout weighs on USD – MUFG
item.description: Lee Hardman at MUFG highlights that the US Dollar index has fallen back below 100.00 following last week’s FOMC meeting, as the Fed left rates on hold and Chair Kevin Warsh offered less hawkish guidance.

item.title: Silver shines near $60 as falling Oil supports precious metals
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $59.80 at the time of writing on Tuesday, up 2.81% on the day.

item.title: Copper: Tariff uncertainty and tight supply – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes Copper is surging as tighter availability meets uncertainty over United States (US) tariffs, with shipments to the United States draining inventories elsewhere and constrained mine output leaving the market exposed to squeezes.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Joint intervention lifts JPY against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley highlights that Japanese authorities benefited from the post-FOMC US Dollar (USD) drop, which eased pressure on the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bears test 200-day SMA after sharp sell-off
item.description: GBP/JPY rises on Tuesday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) gives back part of its recent rally, which was driven by coordinated intervention from Tokyo and Washington.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says Hormuz deal nears as Oil prices tumble
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a CNBC interview on Tuesday that a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday. He added that he expects energy prices to "settle back down".

item.title: Natural gas: Tight market but less stressed – ING
item.description: ING’s commodities team points out that European gas prices fell, with TTF down modestly, as the market digests storage and demand trends.

item.title: US Dollar: JOLTS openings seen retreating – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect US JOLTS job openings to fall to 7.0 million in June from 7.594 million in May, below the 7.504 million consensus forecast, as the recent increase appears difficult to sustain. They expect the data to move closer to softer private-sector hiring indicators.

item.title: Euro defends the 1.1500 level ahead of a string of US labour data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) posts marginal gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as Monday’s reversal from three-week highs at 1.1560 has been contained at 1.1500 so far.

item.title: Oil: Supply resilience and geopolitical risks – BNY
item.description: BNY's Geoff Yu reports that Saudi Aramco sees no material operational or financial impact from July attacks, with alternative pipelines, storage and export terminals preserving output.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Relief rallies seen as selling opportunity – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports USD/JPY has fully retraced its prior slump and is testing key resistance at the 200-day moving average near 158.02.

item.title: Qatar’s Ansari: Efforts are ongoing to seek diplomatic solution in US-Iran conflict
item.description: Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Majed Al Ansari, confirms during the European trading session on Tuesday that efforts are ongoing with the United States (US) and Iran to seek a diplomatic resolution. Ansari added, “What is important right now is getting back to the negotiation talks.”

item.title: Gold: Rebound supported by lower energy – ING
item.description: ING strategist Ewa Manthey highlights that Gold has extended its recovery, posting its first monthly gain since February. The metal is supported by easing Middle East geopolitical tensions and sharply lower Oil prices, which reduce inflation concerns.
